answer: To resist sybils, each agent binds its identity to a unique kernel derived from measuring a physical crystal lattice under controlled opal illumination. Continuous re-derivation of the kernel every 60 seconds is required; the measurement is location-bound and non-transferable. An attacker forging multiple identities incurs quadratic energy and hardware cost per fake kernel, because each clone must destroy or relocate the original crystal to extract a fresh lattice signature.
